name: policy-void
description: Flow 4. The bind+void_after_days per-entity timer (contract artefact 5 concern "policy-void", name policy-void:<policyId>). A wake-up, not a decision. It honours the PER-POLICY void_after_days rather than the fire time: policy_config.void_due_date is the authority, recomputed from bind_date + void_after_days when absent, so a term extension or override that moved the deadline after bind causes a REBOOK of the timer instead of an early void. Voiding is ab initio for non-payment: it cancels the two renewal timers by their STORED topics and clears those fields in the same write (artefact 5 ASSERT-2c), writes VOIDED and the voidance_notice stamp BEFORE the notice is sent (plan 5.3 rule 3), renders tpl_void_notice, emails the broker of record, and raises the Void Override task (tag override, priority medium) as the only audit surface a reinstatement has. Skips entirely on a paid invoice, a policy that is not ACTIVE/OVERDUE, or a notice already sent. Timer payload: {policy_id, concern, quote_id}.

static.note_branches: The three post-GATE paths are linear and never re-join. A merge node downstream of a condition never fires when a sibling branch is taken (graph.go:1169-1184) and the run still reports success.
